listings.title: Stories from the Queer Archives
listings.description: Objects such as banners, T-shirts, and buttons in the Vermont Queer Archives at the Pride Center of Vermont reflect currents and changes in the lives of Vermont’s LGBTQ+ community. Meg Tamulonis, volunteer curator of the Archives, discusses how these objects mark various milestones, from Pride events to legal rulings, and considers why some parts of the queer community aren’t well-represented in the Archives. This is a Vermont Humanities event hosted by Brownell Library and it is inspired by this year's Vermont Read: Charity and Sylvia, a graphic novel by Tillie Walden (pick up a free copy at the program)!

listings.title: Lane Series: Gabriela Martinez
listings.venue: The University of Vermont Recital Hall
listings.description: Venezuelan pianist Gabriela Martinez has a reputation for the lyricism of her playing, her compelling interpretations, and her elegant stage presence. She is a fifth-generation female pianist and began her piano studies in Caracas with her mother, Alicia Gaggioni. She attended The Juilliard School, where she earned her Bachelor and Master of Music degrees as a full scholarship student of Yoheved Kaplinsky. Since her orchestral debut at age six, she has performed with over 100 orchestras and in venues as prestigious as Carnegie Hall, Salzburg’s Grosses Festspielhaus, Dresden’s Semperoper, Copenhagen’s Tivoli Gardens, and Paris’s Palace of Versailles.
